title: 111 files of hand-placed work on ac-box that a deploy will delete
description:
The deploy audit found the box's src tree diverges from git by 59 files that have NEVER existed in git on any branch, plus 52 modified ones. Preserved locally as ac-host branch box-state-2026-09-07 (capture only, deliberately unpushed - reviewable via 'git diff main..box-state-2026-09-07').

The largest piece is an entire 'series' racing feature, hand-placed directly on the box outside the pipeline: shared/series_lib.py, bot/series_cmds.py, bot/series_poll*.py, scripts/generate_series_liveries.py, scripts/publish_series_race_pack.py, scripts/kn5_inspect.py, catalog/series/series-1.json, compose/docker-compose.series.yml. bot/bot.py also carries ~5KB of divergence (52136 bytes on box vs 47072 in git).

Confirmed independently: those filenames appear in no commit on any branch, and no last-applied.json exists, so sync_tree's rsync path has never once run for real. The first real run deletes all 59 and reverts bot.py.

DO NOT run the ops pipeline with DOWNTIME=1 until this is reconciled. Reconciliation is a judgement call per file - which belongs in main, which is scratch - so nothing was merged.

Full detail: ac-host/docs/deploy-audit.md.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: Now BLOCKING .27 and, by extension, every future change that lives in the deployed tree rather than the NixOS closure - compose files, sidecar code, content pipeline. last-applied.json still does not exist, so sync_tree has never run once; the first run deletes 59 files. This has moved from 'important finding' to critical path.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text:
RECONCILED and pushed as ac-host c92180f: 74 files, 9403 insertions. The content plane is no longer a destructive operation.

Taken from the box: the series feature and its dependencies (series_lib, skin_livery, skin_uv, kn5, the bot's series commands and polls, livery/race-number generation, race-pack publishing, catalog data, the compose overlay, and the render_cfg/content_manifest changes its tests need).

NOT taken - this was a two-way merge, not a restore. The box is BEHIND git on 11 files, and a wholesale restore would have reverted every fix from today: .gitignore lacks .env.*, flake.nix lacks the monitoring output, modules/arcade-hub.nix is the mojibake copy, modules/ac-host.nix lacks TimeoutStartSec, pending_deploy.py lacks PRESERVE_LOCAL, and the CI compose lacks cgroup_parent. Verified all four still intact after the merge.

Discarded as Windows-copy debris: ZBy4zK7aiLNl5bKp (50 bytes containing a Windows path), the stale top-level arcade-hub.nix, home-arcade's arcade/metadata/crops and docs/plan-arcade.md misfiled in this repo, and src/state/ - owned by an unmappable UID and mounted by nothing, while containers actually bind /var/lib/ac-host/static.

Two defects that bypassing CI had hidden, both fixed: dejavu_fonts was never declared in the flox manifest so five test_skin_livery cases died on a missing font (verified the manifest entry suffices by simulating flox's XDG_DATA_DIRS), and bot/test_bot.py still asserted the unregistered-user copy names /steam-request when it now points at /intake. Full suite green: 95 scripts, 13 bot, 44 sidecar, 20 shared.

title: The arcade tenant exists only on the box and a content deploy will delete it
description:
ac-box's deployed source tree at /var/lib/ac-host/src has FORKED from ac-host git (both at b7b091a). The entire home-arcade integration exists only on the box and was never committed:
  - modules/arcade-hub.nix: not in git at all (plus a stale top-level arcade-hub.nix)
  - flake.nix: 2 lines exposing and composing nixosModules.arcade-hub, not in git
  - hosts/ac-box/configuration.nix: the whole 11-line services.arcade-hub block (enable, lanAddress, gameInterface, rsync, freeciv, mindustry), not in git
  - the box copy also carries 128 CRLF lines, consistent with having been hand-edited from Windows (same provenance as the mojibake in the vendored module)
Drift also runs the OTHER way: the box's modules/ac-host.nix is MISSING 2 lines git has - a TimeoutStartSec = 15min guard with a comment about a sidecar rebuild hanging and blocking boot. So the box is neither ahead nor behind, it is forked.

THE ACTIVE RISK: shared/pending_deploy.py sync_tree() runs 'rsync -a --delete' (falling back to rmtree + copytree). The next Buildkite content deploy therefore DELETES modules/arcade-hub.nix and overwrites flake.nix and configuration.nix with the git versions that never mention arcade-hub. The running system survives until the next nixos-rebuild, at which point freeciv, mindustry, the samba share, rsyncd and the arcade tmpfiles all disappear. Phase 2's cutover IS a nixos-rebuild, so this must be resolved first.

Also invalidates an assumption in the migration plan: phase 1's no-op cannot be validated against git, because git has never described the running system. The reconciliation checklist and any diff must treat the BOX tree as ground truth.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: Resolved. The arcade wiring is now in ac-host git and pushed: canonical module (not the mojibake copy), the two flake lines, and the services.arcade-hub block, all LF. A content deploy can no longer erase the tenant. Note the audit found this was the first of FOUR instances of the same bug class - see .23 for the largest one still open.

title: homelab has no CI: nothing evaluates .#ac-box on push
description:
Planned as part of phase 5 and never done. homelab has no Buildkite pipeline and no CI of any kind, so nothing automatically evaluates nixosConfigurations.ac-box when homelab or any tenant changes. Every gate this session was run by hand.

That matters more now than it did before: ac-host USED to evaluate a full system in its own flake check, and .25.13 removed that. So the composed host config currently has no automated evaluation anywhere. A port collision, a broken tenant module or a bad lock bump would be found by a human at switch time rather than on push.

Wanted: a pipeline that runs 'nix build .#nixosConfigurations.ac-box.config.system.build.toplevel' plus the modules/tenant/tests eval harnesses. The agent already runs on the box with the Flox/MinIO cache, so the build is mostly substitution. agent-hub has no CI either.

title: Slicing a compose unit does NOT fence its containers
description:
Invalidates the premise of .12 and the modules/ci draft (.19), found while verifying phase 6.

Docker container cgroup placement is decided by dockerd, NOT by the cgroup of whoever invoked docker. Proof: the CI containers were started by a human from an SSH session, which lives in user.slice, yet they sit in system.slice/docker-<id>.scope. Container scopes are siblings of the invoking unit, not children of its slice.

So wrapping the CI stack in a systemd unit and assigning THAT unit to batch.slice would not fence anything. Verified the agent's effective cpuset is 0-55 - fully unfenced, free to take the cores races run on. Also verified: daemon.json sets no cgroup-parent (so dockerd defaults to system.slice), no container sets CgroupParent or CpusetCpus, and no compose file has cgroup_parent, cpuset, cpu_shares or cpus fields.

This means the tiering guarantee currently protects against arcade and agent-hub but NOT against CI, which is the single workload most likely to consume all 56 threads.

Real options, none of which is 'add a systemd unit':
  1. compose 'cgroup_parent: batch.slice' per service - containers land inside the slice and inherit AllowedCPUs.
  2. compose 'cpuset: 28-55' per service - direct, but duplicates the fence rather than deriving it from the tier.
  3. dockerd --cgroup-parent default - fences EVERY container including the race servers, so almost certainly wrong here.
Option 1 is the one that composes with the tier model, since the slice already carries the derived limits. The modules/ci draft needs reworking around it before adoption, and .19's design note should be corrected rather than followed.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text:
Mechanism verified and fix shipped. Proved on ac-box (systemd cgroup driver, cgroup v2) that --cgroup-parent=batch.slice yields cpuset 28-55 while no parent yields 0-55, then set cgroup_parent: batch.slice on all three CI compose services in ac-host 4581df4. homelab now warns when any needsDocker tenant sits in a fenced tier (fires for ci, correctly silent for assetto since critical is unfenced by design), and ADR 0005 records the mechanism plus the two rejected alternatives (per-service cpuset duplicates what the tier derives; dockerd --cgroup-parent would fence the race servers too).

NOT YET IN EFFECT: cgroup_parent applies at container creation, so the running containers keep cpuset 0-55 until recreated. Adoption requires 'docker compose -f compose/docker-compose.buildkite.yml --env-file compose/.env.buildkite up -d' from a PLAIN SSH SESSION - recreating the agent kills the process that deploys the box, so it must never be run through a pipeline step on that agent.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text:
BLOCKED on .22, discovered by trying to adopt it. The compose change is in git (sha 4581df44, and Buildkite has queued it as pending-deploy) but the box's copy of docker-compose.buildkite.yml is stale - 0 occurrences of cgroup_parent. 'docker compose up -d' therefore read the old file, saw no change, and silently did nothing: container uptimes unchanged at 34/44h, CgroupParent empty, cpuset still 0-55.

Getting it onto the box needs a content deploy (ops.yml DOWNTIME=1 -> ci_downtime.py -> sync_tree), and that is exactly what .22 blocks: rsync --delete would erase the 59 files that have never been in git. So the content-plane reconciliation is now on the critical path for any change that lives in the deployed tree rather than the closure.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text:
CLOSED, live and verified. Both CI containers now report parent=batch.slice with effective cpuset 28-55, while the race servers correctly stay at 0-55. Nothing lost in the recreation: all three named volumes survived including the 1.8GB buildkite-nix store, MinIO health returns 200, 13 containers and 3 race servers up.

The fix travelled the full intended path for the first time: compose change in git -> content deploy syncs the tree -> containers recreated from a plain SSH session. The two earlier no-op attempts were the same lesson twice - docker reads the compose file from the box's tree, which only the content plane updates.

title: Rework Slice= assignment to skip non-drainable tenants
description:
PREREQUISITE for phase 6, and the reason phase 6 is not simply next. Slice= is applied when a unit STARTS; daemon-reload will not move a running service between slices. So assigning it to ac-host-static forces a restart, and that unit's ExecStop is docker rm -f - it would destroy the race containers.

The resolution is that critical tenants never need to be in a slice at all: the protection comes from AllowedCPUs fencing background and batch AWAY from the low cores, not from confining races. Change resources.nix to assign Slice= only where quiet.drainable = true, and never for tier = critical. Verify with dry-activate that ac-host-static does not appear in the restart set.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: DONE, committed 5f50ec0. resources.nix now assigns Slice= only where tier != critical AND quiet.drainable, and emits a warning naming the units it skips so the exclusion is visible in the built system. Verified in the fixture: the critical tenant's unit resolves to null while arcade -> background.slice, observability -> interactive.slice, agent-hub -> batch.slice. ac-host-static can no longer be restarted to receive a cgroup label, which is what would have destroyed the race containers.

title: Phase 2.1: apply the Mindustry host/port fix
description:
GATED AND WAITING. home-arcade e82bb75 fixes two further bugs the stdin fix exposed: 'host sandbox' parsed sandbox as a map name (server's help is 'host [mapname] [mode]'), and mindustry.port was decorative while the server sat on its built-in 6567. Verified against the real jar: 'Opened a server on port 16567.'

homelab's lock is bumped and the closure is built: 0bsx7lrpykybr1a7xqp839q8nx7dv935. Gate 1a shows ONLY arcade-mindustry.service differing; gate 2 shows only that unit stopping and starting. Needs: ssh ac-box 'nixos-rebuild switch --flake github:imkarrer/homelab#ac-box'. Acceptance: ss -tulnp shows 6567 listening for the first time.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: DONE 7 Sep 2026 15:06:59, generation 25. 6567 now listening on TCP and UDP. Log confirms all three startup commands executed separately: 'name set to Arcade', 'port set to 6567', 'Map loaded', 'Opened a server on port 6567'. Blast radius exactly as gate 2 predicted - docker, ac-host-static, arcade-freeciv and grafana all still NRestarts=0, 13 containers untouched. First feature delivered end-to-end through the new stack: fix in home-arcade, bump the lock, re-gate, switch.

title: Phase 1: compose and prove the no-op
description: DONE 7 Sep 2026. flake.nix + hosts/ac-box/configuration.nix, enforce all-off, nixpkgs pinned to the box's exact revision c5c4a43. Closure anx183kj built on the box. Gate 1 clean, gate 1a showed 17 file diffs all understood, gate 2 confirmed docker.service absent and ac-host-static under 'would NOT stop'.

title: Phase 2: switch the entry point to homelab
description: DONE 7 Sep 2026 14:55:48, generation 24. Verified: active closure matches the gate-tested path exactly, NRestarts=0 for docker and ac-host-static, 13 containers with uptimes all predating the switch. ac-box's system plane now comes from homelab.

title: Migration phases
description: The eleven-step sequence from docs/runbook-cutover.md and the plan artifact. Findings and one-off tasks live directly under homelab-bqo; this epic is the ordered path.

title: Expose monitoring as a flake output from ac-host
description: ac-host/flake.nix imports ./modules/monitoring.nix by path rather than exposing it, so homelab cannot consume it as an input - and without it the phase-1 closure differs enormously. Clone github.com/imkarrer/ac-host to ~/src/ac-host and add nixosModules.monitoring alongside the existing ac-host and arcade-hub outputs. Do NOT lift or move the module, and do NOT touch its ../scripts/ references: this is a one-line exposure so the no-op can consume it unchanged. Also report whether anything else in that flake blocks consuming it as an input from homelab. Local commit only, no push.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: Done and pushed as part of a05a908. nix flake check passes with nixosModules.monitoring resolving. The consumability report is at ac-host/CONSUMABILITY.md; its key finding is that virtualisation.docker.enable is the only hard option collision with homelab's platform modules, and that it merges silently while both sides evaluate true - a latent landmine rather than an immediate error.

title: No-op reconciliation checklist: live config vs homelab
description: docs/noop-reconciliation.md. Enumerate EVERY setting in ac-box's live configuration (read-only from ac-box:/var/lib/ac-host/src/hosts/ac-box/configuration.nix, modules/ac-host.nix, modules/monitoring.nix, flake.nix) and map each to where homelab reproduces it, or flag it as a gap. This is the checklist a human works through before the cutover, and the thing most likely to catch what the composition silently drops. Pay attention to values that must match EXACTLY (users and their groups, nix.settings, sshd settings, journald, boot loader, nvidia) and to anything ac-host sets that homelab currently has no home for.

title: Gate contract effects behind homelab.enforce so phase 1 can be a no-op
description: The contract as built cannot be part of a no-op: enabling it emits slices, firewall rules, scrapeConfigs and /etc/homelab/tenants.json, all of which change the closure. Add homelab.enforce.{firewall,slices,scrape,inventory}, all defaulting false, gating ONLY the derivations in ports.nix/resources.nix/metrics.nix/quiet.nix. Assertions (port collisions, memory budget, forwarded-justification, mgmt-address) must ALWAYS run regardless of the toggles - they are eval-time and cost nothing in the closure, which is the whole point. Extend the existing test harnesses to cover both states: enforce off still fails on tcp/8091, and emits no firewall/slice/scrape/etc attrs at all.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: Done, committed 1174210. Coordinator re-ran the gates: collision still fails with all four flags false, budget still asserts, slices/firewall/scrape/etc all absent when off, all-true reproduces the prior numbers.

title: CI stack has no systemd units, so the platform cannot slice it
description: Confirmed: no buildkite or minio unit files exist on ac-box. The Buildkite agent and MinIO are started by a human running 'docker compose up -d --build', per the compose file's own header. Consequence for this refactor: ci.units = [] , so there is nothing for resources.nix to assign to the batch slice - meaning the 'a Nix build cannot starve a race' guarantee does NOT hold for the CI tenant, which is the single most likely thing to eat 56 cores. Bringing the CI stack under systemd is a prerequisite for that guarantee, not a nicety.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: This IS phase 9 of the migration sequence; not duplicated under homelab-bqo.25. Its prep task is .19 (draft the systemd module), which was killed by the session rate limit and never redone. Sequencing note: this is a prerequisite for the tiering guarantee actually holding, since ci.units is empty and a Buildkite Nix build is the likeliest thing to consume all 56 threads.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: PREMISE CORRECTED - see the new sibling ticket. Bringing the CI stack under systemd is necessary but NOT sufficient: dockerd places container scopes under system.slice regardless of the invoking unit's slice, so slicing the compose unit fences nothing. The fix has to reach the containers themselves, via compose cgroup_parent pointing at the tier's slice. Verified the agent's effective cpuset is 0-55 today.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text:
REFRAMED and downgraded. The fencing goal is already met by cgroup_parent (see .27) - the CI containers are in batch.slice with cpuset 28-55 despite still having no systemd unit, because container placement is dockerd's decision and cgroup_parent addresses it directly.

So this ticket is no longer about resource control. What a systemd unit would still buy is lifecycle: start on boot, ordering after docker.service, and a supervised restart path instead of a human remembering to run docker compose up -d. Worth doing, no longer urgent. modules/ci/ in homelab is the draft, and its design note about slicing the unit should be corrected - that was never what fenced anything.

title: agent-hub runner uses --network host on a box full of localhost-bound services
description: scripts/run-task.sh:83 runs the aider container with --network host, documented honestly at line 17 as a known gap (rootless dockerd gets no netns on this box). Consequence on ac-box specifically: the container shares the host network namespace, so model-generated code reaches everything bound to 127.0.0.1 - Prometheus 9090, Alertmanager 9093, MinIO 9000/9001, cAdvisor 9102, the exporters on 9130-9132, plus the AC details sidecars on 0.0.0.0:8181+ and the race servers themselves. This is the largest lateral-movement surface in the whole tenancy and it belongs to the least-trusted tenant. Not deployed today (no host imports runner.enable = true, no systemd unit), so this is a gate on deploying it, not a live incident. Options: a scoped bridge network allowing only llama-server + github.com, or run the runner somewhere that is not ac-box.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text:
PREMISE CORRECTED. This ticket (and my earlier reports) said rootless Docker on ac-box forced --network host. That is wrong: ac-box runs ROOTFUL Docker - verified live via dockerd running as root, /run/docker.sock owned root:docker, and no rootless entry under docker info's security options. The WSL2 dev box is the rootless one. The claim came from run-task.sh's own comment, written about the dev box, which I carried forward without checking.

Consequence: a scoped bridge network is genuinely achievable on ac-box, so this was never the unfixable constraint it was described as.

Implemented in agent-hub e7c0f7f + follow-up: runner.network.mode defaults to 'bridge' - a dedicated Docker network plus a DOCKER-USER-hooked iptables allowlist in its own chain (never flushing Docker's shared global chain), permitting only lanAddress:llm.port and GitHub's published CIDRs on 443, default-deny otherwise. mode='host' survives for the single-tenant dev box but a module assertion refuses it unless network.singleTenantHost = true is set explicitly - verified the assertion fires. run-task.sh also runs a preflight canary per task: confirms llama-server reachable AND an arbitrary external host NOT reachable, refusing to run otherwise.

Residual gaps, documented not hidden: DNS egress is not destination-restricted; the container still runs as root-in-container; and the isolation has not been proven live on ac-box, since that needs a write to the box. docs/network-isolation.md section 4 has the manual verification procedure for cutover.

title: agent-hub: reconcile docs with code, follow host nixpkgs, move off 8091
description: In /home/nixos/agent-hub. README claims 'Phase 2 not started' but modules/agent-hub.nix now has a rootless-Docker aider runner accepting a GitHub PAT - reconcile the docs to what the code does and state plainly which of the README's own phase-2 preconditions (sandboxing, scoped credentials, sops-nix, human PR approval) are actually met. Change llm.port default off 8091 (inside assetto's reserved 8081-8096 block) to 8100. Add inputs.nixpkgs.follows guidance for consumers; llama-cpp on the host's nixos-26.05 is version 9190, so verify every llama-server flag used or documented against that build, including --flash-attn. threads should default to the tier's CPU count, not 0. Commit locally, do not push.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: Done, verified. Three commits in agent-hub (nothing pushed): 40c0505 port 8091->8100, 5729c1e nixpkgs pinned to nixos-26.05 with all five llama-server flags verified against the real llama-cpp-9190 build, f230832 honest phase-2 precondition table. Confirmed by coordinator: defaults are now port 8100 / threads 4, only 'gh pr create --draft' exists with no merge path anywhere, and --network host is real at scripts/run-task.sh:83. Two deviations accepted: agent pinned the flake to 26.05 rather than only documenting a follows for consumers (defensible - the WSL prototype now builds what the box deploys), and it reported the tree clean at start though staged work existed, which it appears to have committed as da50e9a; nothing was lost either way. Security findings split into their own tickets.

title: home-arcade: commit real WIP, then drop host-fact defaults
description: In /mnt/c/Users/isaac/home-arcade. First commit ONLY the 5 genuinely-changed files (.gitignore, catalog/games.json, modules/arcade-hub.nix, scripts/test_source.py, windows/arcade-launch.ps1) plus untracked scripts/fetch_mindustry.py and scripts/unpack_win_jre.py - the other 30 modified files are pure CRLF churn, verify with 'git diff -w'. Add .gitattributes with '* text=auto eol=lf' as a SEPARATE commit so the renormalisation is reviewable. Then remove the lanAddress/gameInterface defaults from modules/arcade-hub.nix so they come from homelab.host. Keep unit names arcade-freeciv/arcade-mindustry. Do not push.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: Done, verified. Three local commits in home-arcade (nothing pushed): 9a1a5ea real Freeciv/Mindustry work (exactly the 7 intended files, and it does carry the Mindustry ExecStart stdin fix), 02eb214 .gitattributes + renormalize, 5cd057d the option refactor. Coordinator verification: 'git diff -w 9a1a5ea 02eb214 --numstat' returns only .gitattributes itself, which proves the renormalization introduced zero content changes - that was the risk with this task and it is cleanly demonstrated. Working tree clean apart from .beads/interactions.jsonl. Agent chose required-no-default over reading homelab.host directly, on the grounds that a tenant flake must stay standalone-usable and must not reach into a schema owned by another layer; that is consistent with the README's one-way dependency rule, so accepted. Note for later: commits landed real-changes-first, so commit 1's diffs still carry CRLF noise and want 'git show -w' to review; normalize-first would have been cleaner but is not worth rewriting history over.

title: Declare all five tenants for ac-box
description: hosts/ac-box/tenants.nix. Five entries: assetto, arcade, agent-hub, observability, ci. Derive every port, unit name, state dir and metrics endpoint from the live survey - assetto game 9600x16 + http 8081x16 + details 8181x16 all scope=forwarded with justification (auth sidecar, authOpen=false, requiredRole ac-practice); arcade 5556/6567 tcp+udp + smb 445/139 + rsync 873 scope=lan; observability exporters 9090/9093/9100/9102/9130/9131/9132 scope=local, grafana 3000 scope=lan; ci minio 9000-9001 scope=local. assetto keeps state /var/lib/ac-host explicitly. assetto quiet.drainable=false with busyCheck from shared/server_health.py; everything else drainable.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: Done, committed 0c6b812. Verified: secrets are declared by NAME only (arcade-smb-password, buildkite-agent-token, minio-root-password, s3-cache-*) despite the agent having read a populated compose/.env.buildkite - no values in the tree. Five findings independently confirmed on the box and split into their own tickets (.9 through .12). Agent correctly preserved /var/lib/monitoring as observability's state path on its own initiative, applying the same reasoning as assetto's /var/lib/ac-host.

title: Extract L0 platform modules from the surveyed ac-box config
description: modules/platform/{network,identity,docker,nix,ssh,boot}.nix, reading homelab.host. Docker moves here from services.ac-host (enable if any tenant sets needsDocker). Reproduce what ac-box runs today exactly - do not improve it: fail2ban, journald caps, nix.gc weekly, trusted-users root/nixosuser/ac, systemd-boot configurationLimit 5, nvidia. Source of truth: ac-box:/var/lib/ac-host/src/hosts/ac-box/configuration.nix and modules/ac-host.nix, read-only.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: Done, committed 07ca9b1. Verified: no NIC name or address outside hosts/ac-box/host.nix (the grep hit in host-options.nix is a description string, and the network options carry no defaults at all - checked specifically, since a default there would recreate the drift one layer up). Fetched ssh-keys.local.nix contains public keys only, no private material, and both fetched files are correctly gitignored. Agent hit a real dead end (Nix imports cannot depend on config) and reverted rather than hacking around it, leaving the hardware-configuration import to the per-host composition.

title: Tiers as capacity shares, slices, budget assertion
description: modules/tenant/resources.nix. homelab.tiers as memoryShare/cpuShare fractions; derive MemoryMax from host.capacity.memoryGiB and CPUWeight for proportional sharing. AllowedCPUs ONLY to fence background/batch away from critical's cores - never hard-cap critical. Assert sum of memoryShare <= 0.9. Activation-time check comparing declared capacity to /proc/cpuinfo and MemTotal, warn on mismatch. Assign each tenant's declared units to its slice WITHOUT renaming them.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: Done, committed 29e56e5. Coordinator verified the derived numbers on ac-box capacity (89958/38553/77107/25702 MiB, fence 28-55) and confirmed critical's slice carries no AllowedCPUs key at all. Notable: the agent caught a contradiction in the PLAN, not the code - the starting shares I specified (0.35/0.15/0.35/0.10) sum to 0.95 and would have failed the 0.9 budget assertion specified in the same task. It trimmed background to 0.30, left critical untouched, and kept the rejected 0.35 as a regression fixture. The plan artifact has been corrected to match.

title: Port registry with collision assertions
description: modules/tenant/ports.nix. Expand portRanges, group claims by proto/number, fail evaluation on any double-booking. Derive firewall from scope: local=no opening, lan/forwarded=host.networks.lan.interface, mgmt=mgmt interface (assert it has an address). Require justification when scope=forwarded. Prove with nix eval that assetto http 8081x16 vs agent-hub 8091 fails, and that moving agent-hub to 8100 passes.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: Done, committed 0c6b812. Coordinator re-ran the gate independently: 'nix eval -f modules/tenant/tests/eval.nix collision.messages' returns [ "tcp/8091 claimed by agent-hub.llm, assetto.http[10]" ] and clean.checked returns OK. The central mechanism of the refactor works. Good judgement call included local-scope claims in collision grouping, since a loopback bind still occupies the port number.

title: ac-box platform layer refactor
description: Introduce a platform layer above the six tenants sharing ac-box. Plan: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/61c15556-ccc7-4cc5-994d-a213c669556c — README.md holds the pinned conventions.

title: assetto's busyCheck semantics were interpreted, not verified
description:
hosts/ac-box/tenants.nix gives assetto quiet.busyCheck = 'test ! -e /var/lib/ac-host/maintenance.json', i.e. BUSY whenever the box is not explicitly drained. That was an interpretation of shared/server_health.py, which tracks a maintenance flag and has no direct 'is anyone racing' check - not a verified mapping to actual race state.

Consequence: boxctl plan reports assetto BUSY essentially always, so it will demand a maintenance window even at 4am with empty lobbies. Conservative and therefore safe, but it makes the drain contract less useful than intended. A real check would query the running acServer instances for connected drivers.

title: Put observability on the tenant contract
description:
modules/observability still declares its own ports and its own firewall rule rather than deriving them from homelab.tenants, even though the observability tenant IS declared in hosts/ac-box/tenants.nix and enforce.firewall already opens Grafana's 3000 scoped to the LAN NIC. So that rule is now redundant with a contract-derived one.

Deliberately not bundled with the phase 8 file move, which was kept as close to a no-op as possible. Also the place to reconcile: the tenant declares the exporter ports as scope=local while the module configures them, so the two describe the same thing in two places.

title: ac-host cleanup: host config and duplicate modules removed
description:
Substance of phase 10, done ahead of the rename. ac-host exposed nixosConfigurations.ac-box, and rebuilding from it produced a system with no platform layer, no contract and the old global firewall rules - reverting the refactor silently. docs/runbook-dual-nic.md documented exactly that command, so it was a live trap. Removed, runbook repointed at homelab.

Also removed modules/arcade-hub.nix (the drifted mojibake copy), modules/monitoring.nix plus its dashboards and two exporters (now homelab/modules/observability), and hosts/ac-box/ (vestigial, and a second copy of the services.arcade-hub block). ac-host now exposes one output: nixosModules.ac-host.

Verified the ac-box closure is byte-identical before and after the lock bump, proving homelab owned these rather than shadowing them.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: DONE, ac-host 40e9f48. Verified the ac-box closure is byte-identical before and after the lock bump, proving homelab owned those modules rather than shadowing them.

title: Convert the other eight leaderboard.json writers to atomic_json
description:
shared/atomic_json.py exists and acctl.publish_health uses it (fd075ed), but eight other writers still do truncate-then-write on the same shared file: scripts/ci_publish_pages.py, scripts/seed_github_env.py, shared/series_lib.py, sidecar/plugin.py, sidecar/push_status.py, bot/bot.py, shared/server_health.py. Each is a window where a reader sees a partial file, and any of them that falls back to {} on a read error can still erase the board.

Mechanical per-file change: read_json instead of json.loads(read_text()) with an empty-dict fallback, write_json instead of write_text. The judgement per call site is what to do when read_json raises - skip the update like publish_health does, or fail loudly - and that depends on whether the caller is mirroring derived state or is the authoritative writer of it.

Not attempted alongside the acctl fix deliberately: eight call sites in five files across three services is a bigger blast radius than the one bug that was actively destroying data every boot.

title: Phase 8: lift observability to L2
description: monitoring.nix moves from inside ac-host into homelab/modules/observability/. Its closure references ../scripts/docker_name_exporter.py and ../scripts/udr_fw_exporter.py, so those scripts and their tests must travel with it - that coupling is why it was consumed unchanged as a flake output for phase 1 instead. Also the natural moment to fix homelab-bqo.13, Grafana's globally-opened 3000.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text:
DONE and gated. Observability lifted to homelab/modules/observability with both exporter scripts, their tests and the Grafana dashboard. Verified after the move: prometheus/grafana/alertmanager all still enabled and the five scrape job names unchanged (node, cadvisor, unpoller, udr-fw, docker-names).

Unexpectedly close to a pure no-op: the exporter store paths are byte-IDENTICAL before and after (sxaygc8g...-docker_name_exporter.py). Nix path literals are content-addressed by content plus filename, so moving a file between repos does not change its store path at all - which is why the exporter units do not restart. Only systemd-tmpfiles-resetup differs, from tmpfiles rule ordering.

title: Phase 7: move Docker down to L0
description:
Out of the racing tenant, into modules/platform/docker.nix, enabled by any tenant declaring needsDocker. platform/docker.nix exists and is tested but is deliberately NOT imported yet.

The subtlety, verified experimentally by the consumability audit: two modules setting the same bool to the SAME value merge silently in NixOS and only conflict on differing values. So importing both today is a latent landmine, not an immediate error - it fires later, for a reason that looks unrelated. Run from a plain SSH session, never through the CI agent this would restart.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text:
GATED. platform/docker.nix is now imported, so the daemon is enabled by any tenant declaring needsDocker rather than owned by the racing tenant. Zero disruption: gate 2 shows docker.service not touched at all, because ac-host.nix's own virtualisation.docker.enable = true still agrees with the platform's computed true and NixOS merges equal bools silently. Verified the composed config resolves docker.enable = true.

Left deliberately: ac-host.nix still sets the option. It becomes a hard eval error only if the two ever disagree - if assetto were disabled or its needsDocker cleared. Removing that line is the cleanup that closes the window, and is not needed for the daemon to change hands.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: DONE, generation 28. docker.service NRestarts=0 and still active, 13 containers and 3 race servers untouched - the daemon changed hands with zero disruption because both definitions agreed on true.

title: Phase 6: flip enforce.slices
description: The only enforce flag that restarts units. Blocked on the drainable-only Slice= rework. Even then, expect arcade-freeciv, arcade-mindustry, grafana and the observability exporters to restart as they move into their slices - all drainable, but it is the largest service churn of the four flags. Slice-level limits (MemoryMax, CPUWeight, IOWeight) can change later without restarts; only Slice= membership needs one.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: Unblocked: the drainable-only Slice= rework (.25.8) is done. Remaining churn when this flips is arcade-freeciv, arcade-mindustry, grafana and the eight observability units moving into their slices - all drainable, but real service restarts, so this gets its own switch rather than riding along with the quiet flags.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text:
GATED in closure gs91nqzpmnss5cg92xfi829gv7dnbg6z. Needs one switch.

A serious bug was found and fixed on the way here. systemd.services is keyed by BARE unit name, but tenants declare units with their .service suffix. Keying with the suffix does not error - it silently defines 'grafana.service.service'. The first phase 6 closure carried TEN phantom *.service.service units, no real unit referenced any slice, and dry-activate reported no restarts because nothing real had changed. The slices existed, so it looked like it worked while every resource limit did nothing.

The tests passed throughout because the fixture declared bare unit names, a format production never uses. Fixture now matches production and includes a .timer to exercise the non-service path.

Post-fix verification: arcade-freeciv, arcade-mindustry, grafana and prometheus all carry Slice=interactive.slice; ac-host-static carries none; zero phantom units. Real plan is 10 units stopping and starting across arcade and observability, both drainable, no assetto and no docker. Expect a prometheus scrape gap and a grafana blink.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: DONE, generation 27, verified at RUNTIME rather than in unit files (which is the mistake that hid the phantom-unit bug). systemctl show -p Slice confirms arcade-freeciv, arcade-mindustry, grafana, prometheus and cadvisor are all genuinely in interactive.slice, and ac-host-static is in system.slice as designed. Live cgroup limits: critical 87.9GiB/CPUWeight 500/no fence, interactive 37.6GiB/200, background 75.3GiB/250/AllowedCPUs 28-55, batch 25.1GiB/50/28-55. Races therefore have exclusive claim on cores 0-27.

title: Phase 5: flip enforce.scrape
description: Prometheus scrape targets become generated from tenant declarations instead of hand-written per exporter in monitoring.nix. The entire risk is job-name stability: a renamed job orphans every Grafana dashboard built on it. metrics.nix already reproduces the existing five job names byte-for-byte (node, cadvisor, unpoller, udr-fw, docker-names) and its tests assert that. Not yet dry-activated - do that first, expecting a prometheus reload.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: GATED AND WAITING in closure gira22rwhcvn3s8fp6jd4wqh63xxqkfz (commit 5f50ec0). Phases 3, 4 and 5 are enabled together because their combined gate 2 is: 'would reload the following units: firewall.service' - nothing stops, nothing restarts, nothing starts. Neither docker.service nor ac-host-static appears. Needs one switch.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: Extra validation for scrape specifically: the generated prometheus.yml resolves to the IDENTICAL store path as the hand-written one (1v9r3wc3c4qyqh38v4q8q6hpskcx22yj-prometheus.yml), so metrics.nix reproduces the existing five job names and targets bit-for-bit. That is why prometheus does not even reload, and why no dashboard can be orphaned by this step.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: DONE, generation 26. All 5 prometheus targets still up, and prometheus never even reloaded because the generated config resolved to the identical store path as the hand-written one.

title: Remove ac-host's global firewall rules
description:
The security payoff of phase 4, and the riskiest firewall step. ac-host.nix uses global networking.firewall.allowedTCPPorts for 8081-8096 and 9600-9615, and monitoring.nix opens 3000 globally. Once enforce.firewall provides interface-scoped equivalents, the globals become redundant AND harmful: they are what would expose AC's HTTP and Grafana on eno1 the moment the dual-NIC plan brings it up.

Rehearse while eno1 is still down - that is a free dry run. Verify with ss -tulnp and by having someone off-LAN confirm they can still reach a lobby, since AC's ports are forwarded by unifi_pf.py and a mistake here locks out real players.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text:
GATED in closure s643cdcfkh5994ia3jidwp28qa8ffqwb. Global firewall rules drop 143 -> 78, exactly the 65 expected: 8081-8096, 8181-8196, 9600-9615 tcp, 9600-9615 udp and Grafana's 3000. The 73 interface-scoped rules stay. Gate 2: grafana.service stops/starts (dashboard blink, drainable) plus a firewall reload; no assetto units, no docker.

Implemented as SCOPING rather than removal - ac-host.nix gained a lanInterface option (default enp8s0) and uses networking.firewall.interfaces.<iface> instead of the global lists. That keeps the module correct used standalone rather than depending on a consumer to re-declare its ports, and it is a narrowing rather than a deletion of protection.

STILL NEEDS: verification from outside the network that drivers can join a lobby. unifi_pf.py forwards to the box's LAN address so forwarded traffic should still ingress on enp8s0 and match, but neither the box nor WSL can test that - both reach it via the LAN interface. A phone on cellular settles it.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text:
DONE and verified, generation 28. Live ruleset now has ZERO global AC/Grafana rules and 73 interface-scoped ones. The dual-NIC exposure is closed: bringing eno1 up can no longer publish lobby HTTP, details, the game range or the Grafana dashboard.

Critically, the user confirmed joining via PUBLIC IP after the switch. That settles the one assumption I could not test from the box or from WSL, both of which reach it via the LAN interface: unifi_pf.py forwards to the box's LAN address, so forwarded traffic ingresses on enp8s0 and matches the scoped rules.

title: Phase 3: flip enforce.inventory
description: PRE-PROVEN. Writes /etc/homelab/tenants.json. Its dry-activate output is byte-identical to phase 1's - it touches no units at all, so it is free and can ride along with any other switch rather than needing its own window.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: GATED AND WAITING in closure gira22rwhcvn3s8fp6jd4wqh63xxqkfz (commit 5f50ec0). Phases 3, 4 and 5 are enabled together because their combined gate 2 is: 'would reload the following units: firewall.service' - nothing stops, nothing restarts, nothing starts. Neither docker.service nor ac-host-static appears. Needs one switch.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: DONE, generation 26. /etc/homelab/tenants.json live with 4 tenants.

title: Phase 4: flip enforce.firewall
description:
PRE-PROVEN. dry-activate adds only a firewall.service RELOAD - no restart, no stop. Verified the derived ruleset is a correct superset: AC's 8081-8096, 8181-8196 and 9600-9615 all present and interface-scoped to enp8s0, arcade's 5556/6567/445/873 intact, Grafana's 3000 now scoped, and 11200 correctly gets NO rule because it is declared scope=local.

Note this is purely ADDITIVE. ac-host's global rules remain, so nothing can lock out external players - but the actual security tightening is a separate item.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: GATED AND WAITING in closure gira22rwhcvn3s8fp6jd4wqh63xxqkfz (commit 5f50ec0). Phases 3, 4 and 5 are enabled together because their combined gate 2 is: 'would reload the following units: firewall.service' - nothing stops, nothing restarts, nothing starts. Neither docker.service nor ac-host-static appears. Needs one switch.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: DONE, generation 26. 73 interface-scoped rules present on enp8s0. Confirmed additive: iptables shows both the global '--dport 8081' and the scoped '-i enp8s0 --dport 8081' coexisting, so exposure is unchanged until .25.6 removes the globals.

title: acctl publish_health races sidecar on leaderboard.json
description: acctl.py::publish_health() does a non-atomic, unlocked read-modify-write of leaderboard.json that races against sidecar/plugin.py's atomic writes, and silently persists an EMPTY board if the read ever hits corrupt JSON. It runs on every boot via up-static, so the window recurs. Needs a design decision (lock, atomic write, or single-writer) rather than a quick patch. From ac-host/docs/deploy-audit.md.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text:
FIXED in ac-host fd075ed, and wider than described. publish_health fell back to {} on any read error then wrote that back, so one transient read failure permanently erased every driver's standings - on a path that runs at every boot via up-static. The plain write_text was also truncate-then-write, which is itself how a reader gets the unparseable JSON that triggers the erase, so the two defects fed each other.

Also: NINE files write leaderboard.json (acctl, ci_publish_pages, seed_github_env, series_lib, plugin, push_status, bot, server_health) and nothing in the repo used os.replace or any lock. It was not a two-writer race, it was a nine-writer truncate-and-hope.

New shared/atomic_json.py: read_json distinguishes absent (None) from unreadable (raises), so corruption can never be silently treated as start-fresh; write_json uses a temp file in the destination dir plus fsync and os.replace. publish_health now warns and skips the mirror when the board is unreadable - the health flag is persisted separately by write_flag/clear_flag, so the worst case is a stale indicator rather than lost standings.

9 tests including that a failed write leaves the previous standings intact and no temp files behind.

title: sync_tree has no backup or rollback despite _local_wipe_backup implying one
description: _local_wipe_backup/ appears in RSYNC_EXCLUDES but is a ghost: no code in the repo or on the box creates, reads or restores from it. sync_tree() therefore has no backup or rollback capability at all, despite the naming implying one should exist. Given it runs rsync -a --delete against a tree that has repeatedly turned out to hold un-backed-up state, a pre-sync snapshot would have prevented all four instances of the bug class found today.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text:
DONE, ac-host. sync_tree now takes a pre-sync snapshot via rsync's own --backup/--backup-dir, so anything deleted or overwritten is moved aside rather than destroyed. Snapshots live at <state>/_local_wipe_backup/<timestamp>, a sibling of the synced tree (never inside it, or rsync recurses into its own backups), pruned to the newest five, and a no-change sync leaves none behind.

Two bugs found by testing rather than reasoning: the snapshot root was derived from state_dir() which defaults to a hardcoded /var/lib/ac-host, so every existing caller - which passes only (src, dest) - failed immediately; it now derives from dest.parent. And utcnow() is second-resolution, so two syncs in the same second shared a directory, defeating both the one-snapshot-per-sync model and the empty-snapshot cleanup.

Also worth recording: my first overwrite test proved nothing. Both files were 3 bytes written in the same second, and rsync's quick-check is size+mtime, so it skipped the transfer and never attempted a backup. The test now uses a different size and a backdated mtime.

5 regression tests added. Full suite green: 25 shared, 95 scripts, 13 bot, 44 sidecar.

title: Draft a systemd module for the CI stack (prep for .12)
description: modules/ci/. Draft, do not wire in: the phase-1 composition must reproduce today, and today CI is hand-started docker compose. Read the compose files and .buildkite config read-only from ac-box, and write a module that would bring the Buildkite agent and MinIO under systemd so they can be assigned to the batch slice. Include the migration note: adopting it means stopping hand-started containers, which is a behaviour change needing its own window. Explicitly document the bootstrap hazard - the CI agent deploys the box, so a change that restarts it must never be shipped through it.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: Draft landed and committed, but its central design assumption is wrong - see the new sibling ticket. A systemd unit wrapping docker-compose does not put the containers in the unit's slice; dockerd puts them in system.slice. The module needs cgroup_parent on the compose services before adoption would deliver any fencing. Everything else in the draft (project name, volumes that must survive, the adoption sequence, the bootstrap hazard) still stands.

title: Options for isolating the agent-hub runner's network (prep for .9)
description: In ~/src/agent-hub. The runner uses --network host, so on ac-box it would reach every 127.0.0.1 service on the box. Research and write up concrete options with real tradeoffs: a scoped bridge network permitting only llama-server plus github.com; a slirp4netns/pasta userspace stack under rootless Docker; running the runner off ac-box entirely. Implement whichever is genuinely workable behind a config option that defaults to the SAFE choice, but do not enable the runner anywhere. The 'should this run on ac-box at all' question is the user's, not yours - present it, do not decide it.

title: Relocate home-arcade to a WSL-native checkout
description: home-arcade still lives on the NTFS mount at /mnt/c/Users/isaac/home-arcade, which is what caused the CRLF churn. Create ~/src/home-arcade preserving full history (local clone from the existing checkout - do NOT push, and do NOT re-clone from GitHub, which lacks the three new local commits). Verify the clone has all commits including 5cd057d and that .gitattributes takes effect. Leave the /mnt/c checkout in place but clearly retired (a README marker or similar) - do not delete it; it is the user's data. Report anything still referencing the old path.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: Done by coordinator after the agent was killed by the session limit mid-task. Verified ~/src/home-arcade: all commits present through 5cd057d, origin correctly repointed to github.com/imkarrer/home-arcade, branch ahead by 6, working tree clean immediately after clone with zero CRLF in committed blobs - so .gitattributes took effect. Both retired checkouts now carry a RETIRED.md explaining why and warning against editing (/mnt/c copy e5edb90; the old agent-hub copy likewise). Neither was deleted. agent-hub also ended up duplicated at ~/src/agent-hub by the killed .20 agent - the copies were byte-identical, so ~/src is canonical and the old one is marked retired. Both new checkouts verified to evaluate from their new locations.

title: Grafana's port 3000 is opened globally, not interface-scoped
description: modules/monitoring.nix uses networking.firewall.allowedTCPPorts = [ 3000 ] rather than networking.firewall.interfaces.enp8s0, unlike every other tenant module. It works today only because Grafana binds 192.168.1.50 directly and eno1 is down. The dual-NIC runbook brings eno1 up, at which point the firewall permits 3000 on it. Fix as part of moving observability onto the contract, where scope = lan derives the correct rule.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: State update after phase 4 was pre-proven: enforce.firewall now derives a correctly interface-scoped rule for Grafana's 3000 on enp8s0, verified in the built ruleset. But that is ADDITIVE - monitoring.nix's global allowedTCPPorts entry is still there, so the exposure is unchanged until the globals are removed. Resolution is therefore split: the scoped rule arrives with .25.5, the fix lands with .25.6 (remove globals) or .25.11 (lift observability), whichever comes first.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: Resolved by .25.6: monitoring.nix now uses networking.firewall.interfaces.enp8s0.allowedTCPPorts instead of the global list. Grafana already bound 192.168.1.50, so the global opening bought nothing while exposing the dashboard on any future NIC. Gated in the same closure.

title: Freeciv's real UDP port is 4555 on 0.0.0.0, not the declared 5556
description: Confirmed live: 'ss -ulnp' shows freeciv-server holding UNCONN 0.0.0.0:4555, while arcade-hub.nix opens UDP 5556 on enp8s0 only. So the UDP rule the module writes protects a port nothing listens on, and the port freeciv actually uses is bound to all interfaces and covered only by default-deny. Not currently exploitable (nothing forwards it), but the module's stated intent and the runtime disagree. Decide whether 4555 is needed at all (it is freeciv's LAN announce) and either declare it properly or bind freeciv's UDP to the LAN address.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: Still valid and now more precisely scoped: freeciv binds UDP 4555 on 0.0.0.0 while the module opens UDP 5556 on enp8s0. Worth noting the contract's registry does NOT yet declare 4555, so a future tenant could claim it and the collision assertion would not object - same class of gap as AC's 11200 range, which was fixed by declaring it scope=local.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: Fixed in home-arcade 34906cb and gated. freeciv-server binds TCP 5556 to lanAddress but its UDP socket is 4555 on 0.0.0.0 - the LAN-announce/discovery port, not the game port. The module was opening UDP 5556 where nothing listens while the real port went undeclared. Added a freeciv.announcePort option (default 4555) rather than deriving it, because --bind governs only the game socket so the announce socket stays on 0.0.0.0 and interface scoping is the only control available. Also registered 4555 in the port registry and narrowed 5556 to tcp-only.

title: agent-hub githubTokenFile is not sops-backed
description: agent-hub's README lists sops-nix storage as a phase-2 precondition; githubTokenFile is currently a plain nullOr path with nothing decrypting it. Repo scoping IS met (PAT discipline plus an allowedRepos allowlist enforced in the generated script, with a module assertion requiring it non-empty), and human approval IS met (only 'gh pr create --draft' exists, no merge path anywhere). This is the one unmet credential precondition.

title: Write the cutover runbook and ADRs into docs/
description: docs/runbook-cutover.md and docs/adr/. Runbook: the three gates (diff-closures, switch-to-configuration dry-activate with the acceptance criterion that docker.service and ac-host-static.service must NOT appear, captured surface diff), the T-7d..T+10m timeline, the abort ladder, and the pinned rollback GC root (nix.gc runs weekly with --delete-older-than 7d, so the fallback closure needs nix-store --add-root). ADRs for: platform layer above tenants, tiers as shares not absolutes, state paths preserved across the rename, forwarded as a distinct port scope. Source: README.md and the plan artifact.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: Delivered docs/runbook-cutover.md + docs/adr/0001-0004. Committed as 9f48532 after coordinator review caught four errors: (1) T-0 step omitted the flake ref, so 'nixos-rebuild switch' would have built from the stale /etc/nixos stock template and wiped all six tenants; (2) boot-menu rollback described GRUB, but ac-box uses systemd-boot; (3) gate 1 demanded 'zero differences', which is unachievable since the version label embeds the flake revision - an un-passable gate invites being weakened; (4) GC-root rollback tried to realise a symlink, and the success criteria compared two paths that are identical after a switch. All fixed in the committed version.

title: Metrics generation, drain policy, and boxctl
description: modules/tenant/{metrics,quiet}.nix generating prometheus scrapeConfigs from tenant metrics declarations (job_name defaults to tenant name - changing it orphans dashboards), plus pkgs/boxctl: reads /etc/homelab/tenants.json, runs switch-to-configuration dry-activate, maps changed units to owning tenants, and reports whether the change needs the maintenance window or can apply immediately. Dry-run only; boxctl must never switch on its own.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: Done, committed. Coordinator verified independently: the single switch-to-configuration call site passes "dry-activate" as a hardcoded literal in a list (no variable can redirect it), the other two subprocess sites are the tenant busyCheck and a read-only nix build, and 17/17 unit tests pass when I run them. metrics and quiet evals both return OK. Good instinct pinning the dry-activate wording to switch-to-configuration-ng's real src/main.rs instead of guessing - a parser matching nothing would make the blast-radius gate a rubber stamp that always passes. One inaccuracy in its situational report: it claimed another agent had landed hosts/ac-box/configuration.nix; that file does not exist. Its own deliverable claims all checked out.

title: home-arcade carries an orphaned second beads tracker
description: home-arcade has its own .beads with the homelab-bqo predecessor issues (home-arcade-wjc, 4 issues covering the original freeciv/mindustry work). All of that is now either done or superseded by this tracker, which AGENTS.md declares the single tracker for the whole multi-repo refactor. Two trackers in two repos is how issues get lost. Reconcile: close out the wjc issues with pointers here, or remove that tracker.

title: CONSUMABILITY.md is stale
description: ac-host/CONSUMABILITY.md documents modules/monitoring.nix and modules/arcade-hub.nix, both removed in 40e9f48, and its central finding (the virtualisation.docker collision) was resolved in phase 7. It reads as current guidance but describes a tree that no longer exists. Either rewrite it for what ac-host now exposes - one module - or delete it and keep the findings in the beads history.

title: Install boxctl on the box
description: boxctl is a flake package but is not in environment.systemPackages, so every invocation this session was a bare /nix/store path. Add it to the platform's package set so 'boxctl plan' is available to an operator without knowing a hash.

title: Tier shares are untuned starting values
description: homelab.tiers ships 0.35/0.15/0.30/0.10 memory and 0.50/0.20/0.25/0.05 CPU, described in resources.nix as illustrative rather than measured. Nothing has been checked against real usage: whether batch's ~25GiB is enough for a Nix build of the AC images, whether interactive's 37GiB fits Grafana plus Prometheus retention, or whether critical's fence at CPU 28 matches what the race servers actually use under load. The observability stack now has the data to answer this.

title: boxctl mislabels restarts as 'newly-started units, not disruptive'
description: In boxctl plan output, units appearing in BOTH the stop and start lists are restarts, not new starts, but they are annotated '(newly-started units, not disruptive)'. Seen on the phase 6 plan, where prometheus and grafana stop and start - which means a real scrape gap and a dashboard blink, not a non-event. An operator trusting that label would under-estimate the impact. Fix: intersect the stop and start sets and label that intersection as restarts.

title: Phase 10: rename ac-host to assetto
description:
Deliberately last, and a one-way door. Order: module namespace, then flake output, then the repo with its Buildkite pipeline slug (isaac-karrer/ac-host), its GitHub webhooks, and the CI agent's checkout path.

Code only. /var/lib/ac-host stays exactly where it is as an explicit state.dirs override - renaming code is a commit, renaming a state directory is a data migration of races, series, content and the player whitelist, and there is no reason to buy both risks at once. See ADR 0003.

comments.author: Isaac Karrer
comments.text: Reopened. Was closed in error by a sloppy 'bd close $(bd list | grep -oE ... | tail -1)' that matched the wrong id. Still outstanding: the services.ac-host -> services.assetto option namespace, the flake output name, and the repo rename with its Buildkite slug and webhooks. Note the SUBSTANCE of this phase - removing ac-host's host config and duplicate modules - was already done separately in .25.13; what remains here is purely the naming.

title: ac-host-dev.service is inactive while its containers run
description: systemctl reports ac-host-dev.service inactive/linked, yet ac-host-dev-plugin-1, ac-host-dev-details-1, ac-host-dev-auth-1 and ac-dev-static-dev-blackhawk have been up 33 hours - started by hand, bypassing the unit. Matters for cutover: dry-activate reasons about units, so hand-started containers are invisible to the blast-radius gate. Decide whether the dev stack should be unit-managed or explicitly declared as out-of-band.
